headline: Democrats take the Senate as GOP turns on its own
summary: Democrats ended the Republicans' 53-seat majority, with Ossoff holding Georgia and Talarico beating Paxton in Texas. Republicans began blaming Trump and NRSC chair Tim Scott, and Schumer's leadership came into question.

headline: Conservative voices blame Iran war and gas prices for wipeout
summary: Right-leaning commentators called the night catastrophic for Republicans and pointed to the Iran war, fuel costs and weak candidates. Trump said he would work with the new Congress while keeping his veto ready.

headline: Massie and Greene say broken promises cost Republicans
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie and former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene said Republicans paid for unkept promises on foreign conflicts and transparency. Commentator Matt Walsh called for new party leadership.

headline: Mississippi and Alaska Senate races still undecided
summary: Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom looked deadlocked in Mississippi, while Dan Sullivan held a slight edge over Mary Peltola in Alaska with votes still being counted. Democrats had already clinched the Senate majority.

headline: Democrats flip seven GOP Senate seats
summary: CBS projected Democratic control, with flips in Texas, Kansas, Ohio, Iowa, North Carolina, South Carolina and Maine. Democrats held Michigan, Georgia, Minnesota, New Hampshire and Virginia.

headline: Pulido, Fitzpatrick loss and Iowa sweep headline House flips
summary: Democrats won Texas's 15th, ousted Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick in Pennsylvania's 1st and took three of four Iowa seats. About 75 races were still undecided early Wednesday.

headline: North Carolina extends voting at five precincts
summary: The State Board of Elections added hours at precincts in Columbus, Hertford, Lenoir and Wilson counties after disruptions. Statewide results were delayed about 45 minutes.

headline: Democrats win both chambers; Trump loses Congress
summary: Democrats had won 228 House seats and 54 Senate seats by the AP's count, flipping seats in Texas, South Carolina, Iowa, Michigan and Kansas. The article calls it the first time since 2006 that a Republican president lost both chambers.

headline: Democrats climb to 28 governorships
summary: Democrats rose from 23 to 28 governors and Republicans fell from 27 to 20, with two races uncalled. Winners included Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Deb Haaland in New Mexico and Xavier Becerra in California.

headline: GOP mid-decade redistricting push fell short
summary: Republicans' effort to flip 15 seats through new maps came up short, and Democrats gained at least four seats through new maps in California and Utah. Latino voters swung sharply toward Democrats, according to NBC exit polling.

headline: Jeffries outlines affordability agenda and oversight
summary: Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become speaker, plans to restore ACA tax credits and reverse Medicaid cuts. Democrats also plan investigations of the administration, and he says impeachment is neither on nor off the table.

headline: Lawler concedes NY-17 to Cait Conley
summary: Republican Rep. Mike Lawler conceded, flipping the Hudson Valley seat to Democrats. ABC News projects Democrats will control the House, with Jeffries in line to be the first Black speaker.

headline: Hochul and Lamont win; Booker holds NJ Senate seat
summary: ABC News projected Kathy Hochul over Bruce Blakeman in New York and Ned Lamont to a third term in Connecticut. Cory Booker was also called as the winner in New Jersey.

headline: Missouri voters reject congressional map 62% to 38%
summary: The AP called Proposition A for the no side, so the 2025 map will not take effect in 2028. The map would have split Kansas City into three districts and targeted Rep. Emanuel Cleaver.

headline: Amendment 6 complicates any new Missouri redraw
summary: Voters also approved Amendment 6, which bars lawmakers from passing laws that override referendum results. Some Republicans say a Missouri Supreme Court ruling lets them redraw again, but opponents could force another vote.

headline: Jefferson City passes public safety sales tax
summary: Voters approved the increase 8,020 to 6,382, raising the city rate from 7.85% to 8.1% on April 1, 2027. In Cole County, Republican Mike Bernskotter led Democrat Chuck Steck for presiding commissioner.

headline: Stigall, Alford win mid-Missouri House seats; turnout tops 50% in Boone, Cole
summary: Republicans Chris Stigall in the 6th District and Mark Alford in the 4th were elected. Boone County turnout passed 52% and Cole County reached 52.5% by Tuesday night.

headline: Networks project Democrats will flip the House
summary: MS NOW called the House for Democrats just before 10 p.m. ET, followed by CNN, NBC and CBS. The AP had not yet made a call when the report was written.

headline: Cooper beats Whatley in North Carolina Senate race
summary: Democrat Roy Cooper decisively defeated Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina's Senate contest, per the report.

headline: Andrews projected to win South Carolina Senate seat
summary: Democrat Annie Andrews was projected to beat Republican Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina, a seat rated lean Republican before the vote.

headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia governor's race
summary: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia's governorship, becoming the first Black woman to serve as a U.S. governor.

headline: Senate control still undecided; Democrats lead in TX, MI, ME
summary: Control of the Senate was too close to call Tuesday evening, with Democrats ahead in Texas, Michigan and Maine. A 50-50 split would favor Republicans because of Vice President Vance's tie-breaking vote.

headline: Trump approval at 37% in NYT polling average
summary: A New York Times average of polls put Trump's approval at 37% on Nov. 3, near its low of 36% two weeks earlier. Commentators tied the Democratic surge to prices and the Iran war.

headline: Decision Desk HQ calls House for Democrats
summary: Decision Desk HQ projected a Democratic House majority Tuesday night; Hakeem Jeffries is on track to become Speaker. Democrats needed a net gain of four seats.

headline: Trump says he would become 'Mr. Veto' if GOP loses a chamber
summary: Trump told the New York Post that if Republicans lost a chamber he would act as a heavy vetoer. A Democratic House would also gain committee subpoena power.

headline: DDHQ House call came at 9:09 p.m. ET, with NC-11 and PA-8 flips
summary: Decision Desk HQ projected Democratic gains in North Carolina's 11th and Pennsylvania's 8th districts, both Republican-held, before calling the chamber.

headline: Ossoff projected to win reelection in Georgia
summary: Decision Desk HQ projected Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection in Georgia, and that Democrats held their Virginia seat. Overall Senate control was still uncalled.

headline: Moskowitz holds Florida seat in redrawn Trump+9 district
summary: Democrat Jared Moskowitz won reelection in a redrawn Florida district that Trump carried by 9 points, and Democrat Pia Dandiya was projected to win the 22nd District.

headline: Early Missouri returns show Prop A map trailing
summary: With about 1% counted, 'no' led 71% to 29% on Proposition A, the vote on the Republican-drawn congressional map that splits Kansas City. The AP had not called it.

headline: Broward voting delayed 20 minutes by a faulty safety feature
summary: A malfunction in Broward County's new voting system held up opening-morning voting about 20 minutes and some voters left without casting ballots. Officials called most Election Day problems minor and quickly fixed.

headline: Most Missouri counties had under 10% early turnout
summary: A KBIA survey of county election offices found fewer than 20 counties reached 10% early turnout. Early voters clustered in the St. Louis and Kansas City areas, with far less in rural counties.

headline: St. Louis County early voting hits nearly 27%
summary: More than 173,000 St. Louis County voters cast early ballots, versus about 56,000 in the 2022 midterms. Election Director Eric Fey said the statewide amendments are the main turnout driver.

headline: North Carolina voter guide: Cooper-Whatley and three amendments
summary: North Carolina polls ran 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., with Roy Cooper favored over Michael Whatley for Senate. Voters also decide three constitutional amendments and a rematch in the 1st House District.

headline: Midterms open with high prices tied to the Iran war
summary: Gas and food costs remain elevated amid the Iran conflict as voters treat the midterms as a referendum on Trump. The report also notes the Justice Department's Alaska suit and the push over California ballots.

headline: State legislatures: which chambers could flip tonight
summary: Democrats are targeting chambers including the Michigan and Minnesota houses and Wisconsin's legislature under new court-ordered maps. The analysis counts 28 Republican, 18 Democratic and 4 split chambers entering the night.

headline: Governors: 11 of 36 races rated highly competitive
summary: MultiState flags Ohio as a possible flip, Nevada as the most vulnerable incumbent, and a four-way ranked-choice race in Alaska. Texas is treated as a long shot for Democrats.

headline: 145 statewide ballot measures, from voter ID to abortion
summary: Eleven states vote on voter ID or noncitizen-voting measures, and Missouri, Idaho, Virginia and Nevada have abortion questions. Maryland, Missouri and Colorado have redistricting measures, and Alaska weighs repealing ranked-choice voting.

headline: Trump approval at 35% as Jeffries sets 100-day agenda
summary: An AP-NORC poll has Trump at 35% approval and 25% on the economy, with about 7 in 10 saying the country is on the wrong track. Hakeem Jeffries has outlined a cost-of-living and oversight agenda if Democrats win the House.

headline: Kentucky's 6th District is the first House bellwether
summary: The district, which Trump won by 15 points in 2024, closes early and is rated close. Fox's rankings put Democrats as high as 240 seats and Republicans as high as 212.

headline: Two Dan Sullivans on Alaska's Senate ballot
summary: Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan shares a name with a second ballot candidate, a teacher the Times reported was recruited by Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign; Peltola says she knew nothing of it. The race uses ranked-choice voting.

headline: Flooding moves 21 Florida polling places
summary: Rain and flooding forced 21 polling places in eight Florida counties to relocate, mostly along the Atlantic coast. Officials alerted voters by text, email and posted signs.

headline: Westchester machines reject paper ballots; emergency bags used
summary: Machines in Westchester County, N.Y., stopped accepting paper ballots, so voters used sealed emergency bags. The county says those ballots will be counted and the state attorney general's office is in contact.

headline: Judge Chutkan bars DOJ from sending noncitizen voter lists
summary: Judge Tanya Chutkan ruled the administration must stop sending election officials lists of alleged noncitizen voters, citing risk of confusion.

headline: Judge rejects NAACP challenge to DOJ poll monitoring
summary: A judge ruled against the NAACP's challenge to the Justice Department's monitoring program. The government says monitors will be in plainclothes, unarmed and without arrest powers.

headline: Flooding disrupts voting on Navajo Nation and across Southwest
summary: Flooding affected polling access in Colorado, Arizona, Utah and New Mexico. The Navajo Nation changed several locations and San Juan County, Utah, allowed electronic voting.

headline: Trump's answer on accepting results: only if 'honest'
summary: A week before Election Day, Trump gave a conditional answer on whether he would accept the results. Election law experts say the administration's court arguments in Alaska and California are unlikely to succeed.

headline: Michigan: 2.3 million ballots cast before polls open
summary: About 2.3 million Michigan voters, 31.2% of those registered, had voted by Nov. 2. Polls run 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., and officials warn unofficial results may take time because mail ballots in cities like Detroit must be processed.

headline: Trump predicts GOP keeps both chambers as early vote tops 54 million
summary: Trump said Republicans will hold the House and Senate, while AP counted over 54 million early votes, roughly nine million more than in 2022. RNC Chair Joe Gruters said GOP wins if its voters turn out.

headline: South Carolina: Darline Graham faces Annie Andrews
summary: Sen. Darline Graham, who holds the seat after her brother Lindsey Graham's death, is the Trump-backed Republican against Democrat Annie Andrews.

headline: House stands 219-214 as Democrats need a net three seats
summary: Democrats are targeting seats in Florida, Texas and Iowa, and Hakeem Jeffries has outlined a 100-day agenda on cost of living and oversight.

headline: Missouri voters decide Amendment 3 and Prop A map
summary: Gov. Mike Kehoe made a final stop for Amendment 3, which would ban most abortions, while opponents call it an attack on voters' will. Proposition A would adopt a map likely to elect seven Republicans instead of six.

headline: County clerks expect near-record Missouri turnout
summary: Secretary of State Denny Hoskins projects about 55% turnout, or roughly 2.42 million ballots, just under the 2018 midterm record of 2,442,306. Clerks in Boone and Greene counties expect 57% to 59%, and St. Louis County logged 173,484 early ballots.

headline: $55 million poured into Missouri ballot measures
summary: Spending on the three controversial statewide questions reached $55 million through Friday, with almost $17 million on broadcast ads. The state auditor race is the only statewide candidate contest, so the measures are driving interest.

headline: Missouri ballot: four amendments, Prop A and Boone jail tax
summary: Voters decide Amendments 3, 6, 7 and 8 and Proposition A, the Republican-friendly congressional map, plus Boone County's Proposition L jail sales tax. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. and a photo ID is required, with provisional ballots for those without one.

headline: Vance says Stevens endorsement will help Rogers in Michigan
summary: Vice President JD Vance said Rep. Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers will help him. Stevens lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed.

headline: Governors on the ballot: Florida and Ohio draw national eyes
summary: In Florida, Trump-backed Byron Donalds faces former Republican congressman David Jolly, now a Democrat. In Ohio, Trump-backed Vivek Ramaswamy faces Democrat Amy Acton.

headline: Midterms on pace to be the most expensive on record
summary: OpenSecrets projects about $12 billion in federal spending this cycle, and AdImpact calls it the costliest it has tracked. Wesleyan Media Project puts House, Senate and governor ad spending near $7.1 billion.

headline: Hinson pledges to accept Iowa result, says she will win
summary: Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson said Trump's Dubuque visit helped her portray Democrat Josh Turek as too liberal for Iowa. She said she is confident of victory and will accept the outcome.

headline: Senate stands 53-47 with 11 races deciding control
summary: CBS counts eight Republican-held seats in play, including Alaska, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina and Texas, and three Democratic-held ones in Georgia, Michigan and New Hampshire. In Maine, Sen. Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson.

headline: CBS picks 47 battleground districts to decide the House
summary: Republicans hold a razor-thin majority, and CBS's Battleground Tracker projects Democrats winning 229 seats. The 47 competitive districts are expected to settle control.
